text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Multi-media telecoms network Singapore ONE gets 17 companies and research groups to invest Singapore $115 million to develop services for the network.
- Ex-police detective fined Singapore $20,000 for receiving bribe from gambling den operator.
- First Taiwan ship to sail directly to communist China anchors in Xiamen waters.
- Quintuplets born pre-maturely on April 1 out of their incubators and gaining weight.
- Auckland's customs officials catch four scientists and an interpreter smuggling cuttings of apple trees.
- IPC Corp eyes controlling 70 percent stake in German equipment firm Hagenuk Telecom.
- Cellular operator M1 captures about 10 percent of the market within three weeks of its launch.
- State-owned former monopoly telecommunications company SingTel cuts mobile phone rates to compete with M1.
- U.S. carrier APL, being taken over by local shipping firm NOL, makes net loss of US$9.8 million in first quarter 1997.
- Jakarta Stock Exchange finds more than 100 stock-broking firms involved in "unusual trading activity" in shares of recently-listed Bank Pikko.
- Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange chief says institutional players should dominate the market.
- Singapore benchmark stock index slides 20 points.
- SBS Group turns to hotel and hospital properties.
- Freight Links Express Holdings plans bonus, rights issues to raise about Singapore $90 million for expansion.
